claim_verbatim: Leverage compounds until serviceability breaks. [...] That loop runs until incomes can no longer carry the repayments. Then it stops, and it does not stop gently. [...] Demographic ageing shortens the runway. Retirees draw down rather than borrow. A generation that bought with borrowed money will sell to fund retirement, and the generation behind it is smaller and already carries more debt per head. That creates a cliff under the housing market: fewer new borrowers able to service the price, and more sellers.
context: Section on the Australian housing-credit loop: debt-service ratio 15.7% of household income (peak 18.2% in 2008), household debt 178% of a year's income against 66% in 1988.

claim_verbatim: The gap gets harder to close every year it grows. At A$490 billion, the fix is a shift in where new lending goes. Left until serviceability breaks, the fix is a write-down of the loans already made, and those losses land on the banks, their depositors and the taxpayers who stand behind them.
context: Follows pl-092; argues for reweighting so a home loan and a business loan need closer to the same capital.
